subject: Multi-cloud burst: TIA, SCCs, HSM/keystore questions
messages:
From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@edgehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com, kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com
Cc: EdgeHealth Legal <legal@edgehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Questions on SCCs, TIA evidence & HSM during multi-cloud bursting

Hi Jonas / Kim,

Quick context: we're evaluating Redwood for a pilot where EdgeHealth will occasionally burst inference traffic across AWS eu-west and GCP europe-west. Our legal and security teams want to confirm how cross-border safeguards will work during bursts (SCCs/UK IDTA applicability), and whether Redwood's HSM/KMS approach means customer data ever leaves jurisdictionally scoped enclaves. Specific asks below — a short reply or an evidence packet would be perfect.

Asks:
- Which transfer mechanisms would apply when requests originate in the EU but get routed to a burst region (brief: SCCs or UK IDTA applicability)?
- Do you have an HSM/keystore attestation we can share with our security reviewers (key custody, geo-restriction, split-key behavior)?
- Can you confirm if prefix/KV caching or edge failover can cause personal data to be stored outside the EU, and what controls we can rely on?
- Any recommended language for our procurement team for a limited TIA/DTIA scoping (short summary we can drop into the contract)?

We're trying to scope this for procurement by end of month. If easier, happy to hop on a 30-minute call.

Best,
Sarah Miller
Head of Security Programs
EdgeHealth

[Attachment: sample-EdgeHealth-infra-diagram.png]

From: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@edgehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com, laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on SCCs, TIA evidence & HSM during multi-cloud bursting

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kim (privacy & infra), Laura (legal) and Rishi (infra ops) so we can get the right artifact set and a short written summary for procurement.

High-level answers up front while we assemble artifacts:
- Transfer mechanism: if data is processed in the EU region end-to-end, SCCs will apply in the classic controller-processor flow. For bursts to non-EU clouds we typically fall back on our documented SCC-compatible routing policies + TIA that describes the technical and contractual safeguards (i.e., standard contractual clauses + documented technical measures). If EdgeHealth needs UK-specific language, we can include the UK IDTA/UK addendum clauses.
- Keystore/HSM: Redwood can provide a keystore attestation describing our HSM usage (HSM provider, key origin, and whether keys are customer-managed). Short answer: we support customer-managed keys in an HSM and can provide an attestation PDF for your security team.
- Caching & edge failover: KV/prefix caching is region-aware by default and can be restricted to onshore/EU only. We'll include a config checklist and the TIA fragment that specifies caching behaviors and TTLs.

Action items for us (we'll get these to you within 48 hours):
1) Keystore/HSM attestation (PDF) — Rishi to prepare.
2) TIA/DTIA shortform tailored to a multi-cloud burst flow (word doc) — Laura + Kim to draft.
3) List of routing policies & cache controls with configuration snippets — Kim/Rishi.

If this looks right I can schedule a 30-min call Thursday or Friday. Thanks — appreciate the specificity, makes it easy for us to gather the right docs.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the questions and for the diagram you sent. Attached are three items:

1) Redwood keystore attestation (redwood-keystore-attestation.pdf) — describes HSM vendor (HSMCo FIPS 140-2 L2+), our support for customer-managed keys, and commitments on non-export of private keys without customer instruction.

2) Shortform TIA (tia-checklist-EdgeHealth.xlsx) — we've added an appendix "multi-cloud burst path" that maps the request lifecycle and documents: routing policy, cache TTLs and scoping, and mitigation (no persistent non-EU KV storage unless explicitly enabled).

3) SCCs summary (sccs-summary.txt) — two-paragraph procurement-friendly blurb that references SCCs applicability and optional UK IDTA addendum language you can paste into your DPA.

Summary of technical points you can surface to procurement/security:
- Routing: default is region-first; burst destinations are used only when capacity requires it and are governed by contracts + routing policy.
- Keystore: customer-managed keys remain under EU HSM control; we can provide DMZed attestation and a redacted HSM configuration snapshot.
- Cache: prefix/KV cache is configurable to "EU-only" and default TTLs are short (30s–5m) for cached prefixes that may contain any PII.

Next step: if you'd like we can run the short TIA review with your security team Friday 10:00 CET (I blocked 30 minutes tentatively). Also attaching a HubSpot link to the procurement record (HS-48291) and our shared Drive folder.

Call to action for EdgeHealth: please confirm whether you want: (a) EU-only processing guarantee for the pilot (we'll freeze routing + cache config), or (b) ability to allow bursts that may touch non-EU nodes (we'll surface a variance and additional safeguards). Once you confirm, we'll produce a one-page amendment for procurement.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Ops, Contracts
Redwood Inference
